The Python `shlex.quote` program has been formalized and verified in Lean 4 at [21_shlex_quote.lean](file:///home/user/lean_project/Veribench/21_shlex_quote.lean).

### Summary of Formalization

- **Functional Implementation** ([21_shlex_quote.lean](file:///home/user/lean_project/Veribench/21_shlex_quote.lean#L18-L68)):
  - `safeChars` and `isSafeChar`: defines the POSIX safe character set (`a`–`z`, `A`–`Z`, `0`–`9`, `_@%+=:,./-`).
  - `escapeChar` and `replaceSingleQuotes`: replaces every `'` with `"'\"'\"'"`.
  - `quote` and `benchmark_quote`: implements `shlex.quote` returning `"''"` on empty strings, `s` when all characters are safe, and `"'" ++ replaceSingleQuotes s ++ "'"` otherwise.
  - `unquote`: inverse function recovering the original string from a shell-escaped string.
- **Unit Tests & Property-Based Tests** ([21_shlex_quote.lean](file:///home/user/lean_project/Veribench/21_shlex_quote.lean#L70-L90), [21_shlex_quote.lean](file:///home/user/lean_project/Veribench/21_shlex_quote.lean#L439-L477)):
  - Includes ground unit tests (`example ... := by native_decide` and `#eval`) plus randomized Plausible PBTs and bounded PBTs across all 12 property propositions and `Post_prop`.
- **Properties, Post-condition, and Correctness Theorem** ([21_shlex_quote.lean](file:///home/user/lean_project/Veribench/21_shlex_quote.lean#L197-L494)):
  - Proves all 12 property theorems (`empty_string_thm`, `safe_nonempty_thm`, `unsafe_string_thm`, `unsafe_no_single_quote_thm`, `single_quote_escaped_thm`, `nonempty_output_thm`, `length_ge_input_thm`, `unsafe_or_empty_enclosing_quotes_thm`, `unsafe_length_exact_thm`, `safe_idempotent_thm`, `unchanged_iff_safe_nonempty_thm`, `unquote_quote_thm`), injectivity (`quote_injective`), and the main correctness theorem `quote_correct : Pre s → Post_prop s` with zero `sorry`s.
- **Imperative Implementation & Equivalence Proof** ([21_shlex_quote.lean](file:///home/user/lean_project/Veribench/21_shlex_quote.lean#L496-L550)):
  - Implements `quote_imp` using `Id.run do` and mutable loops, tests it, and proves `quote_equiv : quote s = quote_imp s`.
